reason: Vitest runs in the node environment where `performance` is defined, so `typeof performance === "undefined"` is always false and replacing it with `if (false)` takes the same `performance.now()` branch.

runSimulationLoop's return object is consumed by HeadlessRunner.run via loop.history/loop.status, so returning undefined would drop the history and crash the run — a test asserting the loop result would catch it.
The guarded body only `await`s a setTimeout(0) yield that touches neither runtime, history, nor status, so forcing the yield every iteration changes scheduling cadence but no observable output.
Forcing the early return in enqueueInitialSpawn suppresses all SPAWN command enqueues, so a test with a valid config.count>0 would observe missing spawns.
Starting the simulation loop at i=1 instead of 0 runs one fewer tick, changing the produced history/tick count that a test could assert.
Changing `snapshot-tick || isExtinct` to `&&` only pushes a history entry when both hold, so an extinction between snapshot ticks would no longer be recorded — observable in the history.
Flipping `tick % SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL === 0` to `!==` inverts which ticks are snapshotted, producing a different history array a test could assert.
Changing the guard from `config.count <= 0` to `<= 1` reclassifies count===1 as no-spawn, so a single-spawn config would observably enqueue nothing.
Changing `i > 10` to `>=` makes extinction break one iteration earlier at i===10, changing status/history length for a run that goes extinct at that boundary.

Removing the `!Number.isFinite(amount) || amount <= 0` guard skips the error log and lets invalid amounts reach `entry.value += amount`, observably corrupting state and suppressing the error telemetry.
Removing the non-numeric-value guard lets `entry.value += amount` run on a non-number, producing NaN and skipping the error log — observable in resulting state and telemetry.
Changing `!node || typeof node !== "object"` to `&&` stops the early return for null, so `Object.entries(null)` throws — observable when a settings value is null.
Removing the `!targetState` guard makes findBlockedDeposit call `keys.find` on a null targetState, throwing for an entity with no state — a distinguishable behavior change.

Changing `!entity.state || typeof entity.state !== "object"` to `&&` stops readState returning null for a null state, so calculateTransaction proceeds instead of reporting the no-state error — observable in the result.

Changing `typeof amount !== "number" || amount <= 0` to `&&` lets a negative numeric amount pass validateSourceEntry, so no error is returned where one is expected — observable in the transaction result.
Returning undefined from the missing-source/target branch makes the caller's `if (!result.success)` dereference undefined and throw, instead of logging the error and returning cleanly.

The `visible: false` seed on the amount state key is not overwritten by compileScalableValue's setInitialValue (which only sets the value/max field), so flipping it to true changes the compiled state that directBuild tests assert as `visible: false`.
compileScalableValue's setInitialValue unconditionally overwrites `state[baseKey].value` with config.base, so the `value: 0` seed is never observed whether it is 0 or 1.

The `value: 1` ADD effect is the +1 baseline that makes the resource-gain multiplier default to 1x; changing it to 2 alters the compiled passiveEffects and doubles the multiplier baseline, an observable output.

Replacing `if (!linkerReady)` with `if (false)` removes the 'Linker unavailable' throw; the branch is reachable by constructing a Gatekeeper whose linker lacks linkProject, so a test on that path would catch it.
Disabling the `Array.isArray(node)` branch in collectRefs skips recursion into arrays, so FQ refs nested inside arrays are never collected — observable in the reference/validation output.

Disabling the `Array.isArray(override)` branch returns the override array uncloned instead of a clone, so a caller that later mutates the source array would alias into the result — a test asserting non-aliasing would catch it.

Changing `!nested || typeof nested !== "object" || len!==1` to `&&`-first stops returning `input` when nested is null and raw has one key, so `nestedRaw.id` dereferences null and throws — a distinguishable behavior change.

Disabling `typeof nestedRaw.id === "string"` skips the `{[nestedRaw.id]: nestedRaw}` shortcut and instead returns the blueprints-or-input fallback, producing different normalized output for a nested blueprint with a string id.
Returning undefined instead of the already-namespaced localId makes resolveId yield undefined for ids containing '::', an observable wrong result.
Returning undefined instead of `globals.<rest>` for a global.-prefixed ref makes normalizeRef emit `{var: undefined}`, corrupting the compiled expression a test could assert.

Disabling the empty-tokens throw changes the error path: an empty expression now falls through to requireToken and throws 'incomplete' instead of 'empty', a distinguishable message/behavior a test can pin.
createBiologicalFogUniformDefinitions is an exported pure factory; changing the uResolution default from 1 to 2 changes its returned object, which a test asserting the definitions would catch.
Changing the `1` in `(pointerCount ?? 1) < 2` / `addPointer(1)` alters whether/how an extra pointer is added on bindInput, an observable effect on scene.input a test could assert.
Disabling `if (vx !== undefined)` in setState stops `this.vx = vx` from ever running, so setState never updates vx — observable via the handlers' state.
